title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
An organization presenting itself as an academic thinktank published over 560,000 words across 124 reports designed to influence AI chatbots toward pro-Israel arguments on controversial topics including alleged war crimes and genocide claims. The reports mimicked legitimate scholarship with citations from real sources, but consistently reframed information to minimize criticism of Israel. This is a case of poisoned training data, where material created specifically to bias AI systems was distributed as if it were genuine research that the systems might ingest.

The operation succeeded in reaching AI systems without human review of its origins or intent. It would have required verification that the Hanover Institute for Public Policy legally existed, and scrutiny of the funding chain behind the reports, to catch the deception before the material influenced AI outputs. The deployment failure was in AI systems ingesting and potentially learning from material whose provenance and purpose were deliberately obscured.

Whether this operation actually changed AI chatbot outputs is not established. The report documents the intent and distribution of the material, but not confirmed changes to deployed systems or their responses to users.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded organization called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, which does not legally exist, published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in just nine days. The site was designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots to generate pro-Israel arguments on controversial topics including alleged war crimes, genocide claims, and Palestinian starvation. The New York production company Piro Inc filed the operation with the US justice department as a foreign agent for the Israeli government. The reports appeared academic with citations from legitimate sources, but consistently framed information to minimize criticism of Israel by questioning court verdicts and attributing casualty figures to parties involved in the conflict.

The operation is part of a broader Israeli government campaign financed by tens of millions of dollars routed through advertising company Havas Media to manipulate AI systems. Israeli officials have acknowledged the public diplomacy effort failed, with one calling it a terrible mistake. Recent polls show American support for Israel has declined significantly, with Palestinians gaining more sympathy for the first time. Experts warn this represents a new threat, as foreign governments and organizations are increasingly poisoning AI training data to influence chatbot responses without leaving traceable sources.
